source.title: A Technical Report for Polyglot-Ko: Open-Source Large-Scale Korean Language Models
source.authors: H. Ko; Kichang Yang; Minho Ryu; Taekyoon Choi; Seung-Hyeon Yang; Jiwung Hyun; Sung-Yeon Park; Kyubyong Park

record.tranche_reason: The study compares downstream benchmark performance across model sizes, a different measure from pretraining loss that bears on downstream predictability with scale.
record.gate_note: The study reports benchmark scores for multiple models, shot counts, and tasks. Rows below retain Polyglot-Ko results relevant to downstream performance and scale, including SentiNeg prompt variants and WiC. Table 3–5 comparator-model scores and the 0-, 10-, and 50-shot COPA, HellaSwag, and BoolQ Polyglot-Ko scores are not included; these do not change the retained 5-shot trend evidence.
record.test_reason: A model-release report on four Korean Polyglot-Ko sizes (1.3B–12.8B). Its own KOBEST scores across sizes bear on whether downstream performance improves with scale (V6) in a new language setting. The authors state 5-shot performance improves with compute (Figure 2). There is no fit, forecast or loss-to-task mapping, so this is a T3 descriptive size-series test, not T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The paper's main conclusion is that Polyglot-Ko is competitive with or better than other public Korean models on KOBEST. The scaling statement, that 5-shot performance improves with compute, is a brief observation tied to Figure 2. The authors also note the default SentiNeg prompt is unstable, especially at 0-shot, and that all models perform at random on WiC.
record.recipe_differences: Reports downstream benchmark performance across Korean model sizes rather than fitting held-out pretraining loss scaling laws or computing an optimal parameter/token allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: SentiNeg outcomes vary substantially with prompt design; the authors state the default prompt produces instability, particularly in zero-shot evaluation.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. The authors describe SentiNeg default-prompt results as unstable and WiC performance as random across models. The reported scale-related downstream comparison is a 5-shot benchmark trend, not a predictive extrapolation test.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted comparator-model rows from Tables 3–5 and Polyglot-Ko scores at 0, 10, and 50 shots for COPA, HellaSwag, and BoolQ. Retained the 5-shot size series for those tasks, plus all SentiNeg prompt/shot and WiC size/shot results, within the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Whether improvement is predictable: there are no fitted trends, no forecasts from smaller models, and no relation between downstream scores and pretraining loss. Only four sizes are tested, with no uncertainty estimates.
Pretraining loss versus parameters, data or compute is not reported.
No compute-optimal allocation analysis; token counts were set by resource limits.
There is no comparison of shapes at a fixed parameter count.
No non-text or other training-regime scaling.
No exponents are fitted or compared.

record.verdict_notes: Scale here is confounded: the models were trained on different token counts (213B, 219B, 172B, 167B), and the 1.3B and 3.8B models were early-stopped before the epoch boundary. 'Compute' therefore tracks parameters only loosely. The omitted Polyglot-Ko series (declared in rows_left_out) are not uniformly monotone, contrary to the reader's gate note: HellaSwag 0-shot (5.8B 0.598 vs 12.8B 0.595) and 50-shot (0.621 vs 0.612), and BoolQ 50-shot (flat at 0.404 from 1.3B to 3.8B). These would add mild limits_scope evidence. A one-model-family, four-point descriptive trend is weak evidence for 'predictable' improvement.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute; power-law form and range.
Prediction of larger-run loss from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its scaling with compute.
Architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count.
Power laws outside standard text pretraining.
The study evaluates benchmark scores across model sizes, but does not forecast downstream scores from smaller runs or relate downstream performance to pretraining loss.
No scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal split are fitted or compared; prompt changes are not tests of fit dependence.

relationships.condition: Polyglot-Ko, 5-shot on COPA, HellaSwag, BoolQ and SentiNeg; SentiNeg original prompt at 10 and 50 shots; modified prompt at 5, 10 and 50 shots
relationships.reason: F1 rises with model size in each of these series, monotone or nearly so (r01–r16, r21–r28, r33–r44).
relationships.display_finding: F1 increased monotonically or nearly monotonically with model size in every specified series.

relationships.condition: SentiNeg at 0 shots, with both the original and the modified prompt
relationships.reason: With the original prompt, F1 falls from 0.679 to 0.339 between 1.3B and 5.8B, then jumps to 0.912. With the modified prompt it is flat (0.878–0.942). The size trend depends on prompt and shot count (r17–r20, r29–r32).
relationships.display_finding: Original-prompt F1 fell from 0.679 to 0.339 between 1.3B and 5.8B before jumping to 0.912, whereas the modified prompt stayed relatively flat at 0.878–0.942.

relationships.reason: Accuracy stays near chance (0.479–0.506) at every size from 1.3B to 12.8B, with no improvement with scale (r45–r60).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy remained near chance at 0.479–0.506 across 1.3B–12.8B models without improvement from scale.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Polyglot-Ko on KOBEST COPA, HellaSwag, BoolQ and SentiNeg with 5-shot prompts
reader_labels.reason: Scores rise with model size across the reported 5-shot Polyglot-Ko series for these tasks (r01–r16).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: SentiNeg across shot counts and prompt variants, and WiC across tested shot counts
reader_labels.reason: SentiNeg results vary with shot count and prompt; the authors report WiC performance as random across models, rather than reliably improving with size (r17–r60).
